first_impression.reaction: My daughter sent me this, so I'll read it properly. It's a spreadsheet page, really meant for her, but the intro is plain English and it mentions flights, accommodation and visa letters, which is the part that worries me with the family flying over. No silly slang, short paragraphs. I kept going.

journey.quote: Ours downloads as an Excel file with no sign-up, opens in Google Sheets as well, and carries the travel columns a destination wedding needs: flights, arrival and departure, accommodation and visa letters.
journey.reaction: Good. I don't have to hand my email over to get it, and it's thought about people travelling, not just a local reception.

journey.quote: Access needs. Steps, seating, quiet space, anything that helps a guest enjoy the day.
journey.reaction: I'm glad it's there at all. My mother uses a walking frame and nobody ever thinks of her until the day. But it's one line. I'd like it to say outright that walking frames and wheelchairs belong in this column, and that you should ask early.

journey.quote: A preference changes a plate; an allergy changes how the kitchen works.
journey.reaction: Sensible. That's the kind of practical thinking I like to see.

journey.quote: Transport to venue needed. Yes or No, so you have the number of people who will need a way to reach the venue once you start planning that part of the weekend.
journey.reaction: A yes or no doesn't tell you that Auntie can't manage a long walk from the car park. It should point back to the access column.

journey.quote: Visa rules belong to each guest. Every guest should get the right visa for the countries they are visiting or transiting through, and check with the embassy or consulate of the destination before they travel, as Smartraveller advises.
journey.reaction: Clear about who is responsible, and it quotes the government site. I'll forward that bit to my brother.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: Payments and one point of contact is what I want to hear. But it doesn't say who that person is or how I'd reach them, or what happens with deposits.

journey.quote: For a parent chasing one side of the family, copy the names and reply columns into a separate file rather than handing over every address.
journey.reaction: That's me, chasing my side. Fair enough that I don't need everyone's address, and it isn't put in a way that makes me feel like a nuisance.

journey.quote: This is general information as at November 2026, not legal advice.
journey.reaction: Honest and dated. I trust a page that says what it isn't.

journey.section: When a spreadsheet stops being enough
journey.quote: For couples whose guest list is turning into a travel plan, Wedded Concierge puts one Wedded Advisor beside you to plan the whole weekend.
journey.reaction: It's all addressed to the couple. I'm paying half. I'd like a hint that families helping pay are welcome on the call.

journey.section: Planning the weekend around your guests
journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD for Australian couples, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: Now we're talking. Australian dollars, fee in writing before anything starts. That's exactly what I'd ask on the phone.

journey.section: Planning the weekend around your guests
journey.quote: Every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Good. Still nothing about deposits or who is accountable if a supplier over there falls through, but this is a spreadsheet article so I won't hold it too hard against them.

unanswered_questions: Is the deposit protected if an overseas supplier goes under or disappears?
Who do I ring if something goes wrong at 2am Italian time? Is there a named person and a phone number?
Can I, as the parent paying half, be on the first call with my daughter?
Are contracts with overseas suppliers in English and in Australian dollars, or only the Wedded Wonderland quote?
Is there any advice on travel insurance or medical cover for older guests travelling to the wedding?

turn_offs_found.quote: When you are ready to talk it through, start with [Wedded Concierge]
turn_offs_found.why: Every call to action speaks to the couple only. The person co-signing the cheque isn't acknowledged anywhere in the sales part.

would_share_with: My husband, with the closing paragraph about fees in writing and AUD quotes
My brother, about the visa paragraph, since his family are coming from overseas

cta_reaction.quote: A Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD for Australian couples, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
cta_reaction.why: The closing paragraph says the right things about money in writing. But I want a phone call with a named person before anything is booked, and I'd only click if my daughter suggested it. It's her page more than mine.

top_3_changes: Make the access column speak to older and less mobile guests. old: "- **Access needs.** Steps, seating, quiet space, anything that helps a guest enjoy the day." new: "- **Access needs.** Steps, seating, quiet space, a walking frame or wheelchair, anything that helps a guest enjoy the day. Ask early, so the answer is known before the venue and transport are settled."

Tie transport back to access needs. old: "- **Transport to venue needed.** Yes or No, so you have the number of people who will need a way to reach the venue once you start planning that part of the weekend." new: "- **Transport to venue needed.** Yes or No, so you have the number of people who will need a way to reach the venue once you start planning that part of the weekend. If a guest also has an entry under Access needs, read the two together."

Acknowledge the family helping to pay in the closing call to action. old: "When you are ready to talk it through, start with" new: "When you are ready to talk it through, on your own or with the family helping you plan, start with"

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Margaret (mother of the bride, paying half, reading on iPad)
No invented brand facts; missing information listed as unanswered questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments ignored
Suggested edits are exact old/new strings and add no prices, statistics, 'free', vendor names, fees, on-the-ground staff, room blocks, availability, or Advisor management of guest list or visas
Payload matches 07-icp schema (top_3_changes max 3, scores 1 to 5)

open_questions.question: Deposit protection and a named point of contact are this persona's biggest trust gaps, but they are not published in the draft. Should a future brand page or Concierge page answer them rather than this template article?

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link her daughter sent her and is reading on an iPad, per the persona card.
Persona is provisional and not calibrated with CRM data.
